page: Microsoft Azure D4s_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The processor includes Hyper-Threading and features a 260 MB L3 cache. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable for external disk attachments.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2166.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 31.34 GB/sec. However, multi-core scaling is relatively weak, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 3990.58 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 26.13 GB/sec. Memory read bandwidth is also a bottleneck, registering at 36.73 GB/sec for large blocks and 311.23 GB/sec for cached small blocks, both placing in the bottom 25% of benchmarks. Conversely, write operations and database operations perform at average levels, with Passmark database operations scoring 2863.53.

The D4s_v6 offers a balanced hardware profile for general-purpose workloads, but the lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached Premium Storage. The instance is suited for workloads that prioritize single-threaded execution speed over massive parallelization, such as lightweight web serving, text processing, and basic database operations. It is less optimal for memory-intensive read operations, software compilation, or large-scale multi-threaded processing due to its lower multi-core and memory read bandwidth benchmarks.
